newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs posts record first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs posts record first-half profit.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co said Wednesday that pre-tax earnings for the first half of its fiscal year were a record $1.52 billion, up 19 percent from the $1.27 billion it earned in the same period last year reflecting strong performances across the company's business lines.

In a statement outlining results for the quarter, Goldman Chief Financial Officer John Thain said the privately-held investment bank's revenues for the six-month period totalled $3.63 billion, up from $3.13 billion a year ago. Expenses climbed to $2.12 billion from $1.86 billion.

"The results for the first half reflect a record pace of performance driven by merger activity in the investment banking area and strong results in fixed income, foreign exchange and equities," Thain said.

Goldman Sachs, a privately held investment bank, released ony basic information regarding its results. In its first quarter, the firm reported pre-tax earnings of $905 million, up from $565 million a year ago.
Second-quarter highlights for the company included its handling of a $2 billion block trade in British Petroleum Co. Plc shares, the largest block trade in history.
Goldman was also lead underwriter on Hartford Life Inc.'s initial public offering in May.

Employment at the firm increased to about 9,500 worldwide, up from about 9,000 at the end of the first quarter. Capital rose to $5.6 billion, up from about $5.4 billion at the end of the first quarter. Goldman's second quarter ended May 31.
